subject: genetics
question: **Type:** pedigree The parents in the pedigree are unaffected and not related, and their son has Tay Sachs disease. What is the probability that his unaffected sister is a carrier of Tay Sachs disease? ```text PEDIGREE: Generation I: I-1 unaffected male; I-2 unaffected female, partners Generation II: II-1 affected male with Tay Sachs disease; II-2 unaffected female, siblings Key inference: Both parents are unaffected yet have an affected child, the signature of autosomal recessive inheritance, so both parents are obligate carriers. Most consistent mode: autosomal recessive ```
explanation: Tay Sachs disease is autosomal recessive (*HEXA*, hexosaminidase A loss), so both parents are obligate carriers and the sibship genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 (sums to 4). Because the sister is unaffected, the aa class is excluded, leaving three genotypes of which two are carriers, giving 2/3. A is the risk of an affected child, B fails to condition on the sibling being unaffected, and D is the probability of being unaffected at all.
